narrative:
The model determined that you have a 38% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the level of savings you have, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account status had the largest impact and pushed the decision toward denial. Having a balance below zero is relatively uncommon among approved applicants (only 12.6% of them show a negative balance), and the model sees this as a clear warning sign of higher risk.

Your lack of savings worked in the opposite direction. While having unknown or no savings is fairly common (33% of approved applicants fall into this category), the model interpreted your situation as slightly reducing the risk compared with many other applicants. The purpose of the loan (listed as "others") also pulled the prediction somewhat toward approval, as this category is rare among both approved and denied cases.

Even though two of the top factors leaned slightly in your favor, the negative signal from your checking account was strong enough to outweigh them and drive the overall prediction above the approval line.

You should focus on building a positive checking account balance over the next few months, then reapply. This single change is likely to have the biggest effect on improving your chances.
